subject: Liability carve-outs, prohibited-testing exception and remedy alignment
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@brightretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Procurement and legal at BrightRetail reviewed the MSA and we have two items blocking signature:

1) Prohibited / benchmarking testing: our engineering team needs explicit carve-outs that allow limited benchmarking and performance testing (we frequently run load tests as part of integrations). The current "prohibited testing" language reads too broadly and would prevent that.

2) Remedies / damages: our counsel is pushing for injunctive relief + no cap for IP infringement or confidentiality breaches. They are uncomfortable with a flat cap that would apply even when IP or trade secrets are at risk.

I've attached an updated order form that highlights the sections (OrderForm_BrightRetail_2026.pdf). Can we set a quick sync with your legal team? We need both items closed this week to make the renewal cycle.

Best,
Marta
Marta Alvarez
Sr. Director, Procurement — BrightRetail Inc
attachments: OrderForm_BrightRetail_2026.pdf

Date: 2026-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear notes and the marked-up order form. Looping Rishi (GC) and Laura (legal intake/ops) to triage. Quick note from my side: BrightRetail is a strategic account and we want to avoid a long vendor review. Happy to host a 30-minute call with our legal team today or tomorrow to align on acceptable guardrails for benchmarking.

Proposed agenda for the sync:
- Clarify what BrightRetail’s engineering team needs for benchmarking (scope, duration, test accounts)
- Walk through the specific liability carve-outs you requested and any IP/confidentiality concerns
- Agree on redline approach (narrow injunctive exception vs. uncapped damages for specific breaches)

Laura/Rishi — can you review the attached order form and flag any non-starters before we meet?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@brightretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Karthik / Marta — thanks for flagging. I reviewed BrightRetail’s marked-up Order Form and the MSA. High-level legal position (quick summary):

1) Prohibited testing / benchmarking: we are open to a narrowly-scoped exception that allows benchmarking/perf testing provided it is: (a) non-destructive (no data exfiltration), (b) runs against a designated test tenant or synthetic dataset, (c) scheduled with prior notice (48 hours), and (d) subject to a maximum concurrent connection threshold. This preserves our security posture while enabling legitimate integration testing.

2) Remedies & damages: we cannot accept unlimited/uncapped liability across the board. Standard approach we recommend:
   - Carve out uncapped liability for gross negligence and willful misconduct (including deliberate IP infringement or intentional data exfiltration).
   - For confidentiality/PII breaches, allow injunctive relief plus a damages remedy but maintain a contractual cap for ordinary negligence (e.g., 3x net fees).
   - For benchmarking violations (i.e., carrying out prohibited testing), injunctive relief is the appropriate remedy (stop-the-harm). We should resist turning every prohibited-testing incident into an uncapped damages claim unless there is demonstrable loss tied to IP theft or material data loss.

Proposed redline snippet (for MSA Section 9 / Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither party’s aggregate liability to the other for claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall exceed three (3) times the fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the preceding twelve (12) months, except that (i) liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence shall not be so limited, and (ii) either party may seek injunctive relief to prevent or remedy unauthorized use of intellectual property or confidential information."

I attached a tracked-redline (MSA_redlines_v3.docx) with suggested language for both the MSA and Order Form. Key ask for BrightRetail: confirm whether benchmarking will involve production data or only synthetic/test datasets. If they insist on production data for performance fidelity, we will need additional safeguards (encryption, audit logs, and SCC approval).

Happy to take this on the call.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_redlines_v3.docx

From: Priyanka Singh <psingh@baxterlaw.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@brightretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Rishi / team — thank you for the quick review. BrightRetail’s position (from counsel): we need to preserve the ability to obtain equitable relief (injunctive) and do not want a damages cap to apply where there is misappropriation of our trade secrets or willful breach of confidentiality or IP provisions.

Specific asks from BrightRetail:
- No cap where a party is found to have misappropriated trade secrets or engaged in willful IP infringement.
- For benchmarking exceptions: allow controlled testing against production APIs when necessary for validation, subject to NDA-grade controls and a pre-test checklist.
- Please provide SOC2 / security attestation and any runbooks that describe how Redwood monitors and isolates test traffic. We will need that evidence before approving a production-targeted benchmarking exception.

We appreciate Rishi’s compromise language but require confirmation on the SOC2 evidence and concrete controls for test accounts.

Priyanka Singh
Counsel, Baxter & Co. (representing BrightRetail Inc.)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@brightretail.com>, Priyanka Singh <psingh@baxterlaw.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Thanks all — good discussion points. To keep momentum, proposing the following pragmatic compromise that we can capture in a single clean redline:

1) Benchmarking / testing exception (Order Form):
   - BrightRetail may perform benchmarking and non-destructive performance testing provided the tests: run against a designated test namespace or synthetic dataset by default; otherwise, production-targeted tests require (i) prior written approval from Redwood (48-hour notice), (ii) mutually-agreed test plan, and (iii) use of a segregated test API key with rate limits.
   - Any breach that results from an approved test plan will be handled under standard indemnity / breach provisions; unapproved or malicious testing may trigger injunctive relief and potential damages if there is demonstrable loss.

2) Remedies / damages (MSA Section 9):
   - Aggregate cap: three (3) times fees paid in the prior 12 months, except:
       a) No cap for liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence;
       b) No cap for proven misappropriation of trade secrets or intentional IP theft;
       c) Injunctive relief remains available to both parties to prevent unauthorized use of intellectual property or confidential information.

3) Evidence / security: Redwood will provide current SOC2 summary report and a short runbook describing test account isolation and monitoring (I will share redwood-soc2-evidence.zip with your counsel).

Next steps: Rishi / Laura — if that matches legal’s view, we’ll produce a clean redline and a one-page runbook. Marta / Priyanka — can you confirm whether BrightRetail will accept the default synthetic/test-data approach for the initial rollout? If yes, we’ll avoid the production-targeting approvals and move faster.

I can carve out time for a 30-minute call tomorrow afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@brightretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Singh <psingh@baxterlaw.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and testing

Karthik / team — that compromise looks reasonable and is close to what we can sign off on. Two quick confirmations:

1) BrightRetail will accept synthetic/test-data for the initial rollout. If we need production fidelity later, we will submit a formal test plan and request approval as you outlined.
2) Please share the SOC2 summary and the runbook. Also, once we have your clean redline, we will route it internally for final approval and expect to be ready to sign within 48 hours. Could you also send the DocuSign link for the order form when the redline is ready?

Appreciate the responsiveness — happy to jump on a short call if any of these items are contentious.

Best,
Marta
